title: [WIP] Serialization doesn't respect insertion order for Dictionary type.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.4.1.rc1.mono.official [daa4b058e]

*\* Need to test older versions, I'll update them asap.*

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.rc1.mono - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700H (20 threads)

### Issue description

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aba274b1-5e94-49d3-a824-6de77d51fa0e)

I don't think Dictionary is order-dependent data, but I found an inconsistency between the runtime and the serialization logic.

I noticed that key-value pairs were entering the Dictionary in a sequential order that was processed at runtime, but the moment they were serialized, they were sorted by key value.

May related below issues.
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/82234
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/1310 (It's from 2015, I know...)

### Steps to reproduce

- Create resource script.
- For quick test, add `@tool` annotation and put dictionary modification codes inside of `_init`
- Create resource of it and save them
- You can see serialized dictionary are stored as sorted by key, runtime doesn't.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[serialization-not-respects-dictionary-insertion-order.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19407203/serialization-not-respects-dictionary-insertion-order.zip)

- Open it
- Right click File System dock directly to create resource
- Create `TestResource` type resource
- Save it
- Check between output and serialized `*.tres` file
